sentences.text:
This is the fourth bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 o f Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.64/2024 registered at Police Station- Bhangarh, District- Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 365,
376(D)(A), 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 and 5(n) and (g)/6 of the POCSO Act.

The applicant is in custody since 21.03.2024.
2.

Applicant's earlier three bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 24.05.2024, 09.12.2024 and 25.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.Nos.19100/2024, 45265/2024 and 2790/2025.
3.

Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that the victim (PW-1) in her cross-examination has clearly admitted in Para Nos.5 and 6 that there was dispute between her parents and the parents of the accused person.

Multiple complaints were lodged by the complainant before the police authorities and with certain changes, this fact has also been admitted by the father of the victim that there is dispute with the applicant and father of the applicant.

DNA report is negative NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36835 2 MCRC-26647-2025 regarding the co-accused-Dev Bansal and there is allegation that this accused caught hold the victim while another was committing sexual assault.
Hence, it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
4. Learned counsel for State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that no case for bail is made out.
Hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

5. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that trial will take time to be concluded, within stipulated period not completed (as per the order passed in M.Cr.C.No.45265/2024) and also the age of the applicant, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail, hence, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant- Rajkumar Bansal shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.

8. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
9.

Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
C.C. as per rules.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE VB*
